classification.difficultyReason: Interpret each point pattern and connect it to prediction reliability: sparse, widely scattered observations provide weak evidence, while a flattening curve makes the supplied straight-line model unsuitable.

content.prompt: State the problems with making predictions using the lines of best fit in the following scatter plots.

spec.description: Five scattered points and an upward straight line; unlabelled axes with arrowheads, no ticks or grid. Drawing coordinates reproduce relative positions only.
spec.mathematics: Sparse observations with large vertical scatter about the supplied straight line.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied points and the straight line remain visible in the question.

answer.short: There are too few points to establish a reliable relationship. Any association appears weak, so predictions would be unreliable.
answer.worked: Only five observations are shown, and they are widely scattered about the supplied line. There is insufficient evidence of a reliable linear relationship, so predictions using this line would be unreliable.

spec.description: Increasing curved point pattern that flattens to the right, crossed by a rising straight line. Unlabelled axes with arrowheads, no ticks or grid. Drawing coordinates reproduce relative positions only.
spec.mathematics: The observed relationship is nonlinear; the supplied straight line rises above the rightmost observations.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied points and the straight line remain visible in the question.

answer.short: The relationship is nonlinear, so a straight line is inappropriate for making predictions.
answer.worked: The points follow an increasing curve that flattens towards the right. The straight line does not follow this changing trend and lies above the rightmost observations, so predictions from a linear model would be inappropriate.
